runs.name: Cleveland-Cliffs Inc.; formerly Cliffs Natural Resources Inc. to 2017; AK Steel and ArcelorMittal USA 2020, Stelco 2024-11-01; 75M shares sold 2025-10-31; no split
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$12.86** (quote of 2026-10-13 through `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **570,540,047**, one class (10-Q cover at 2026-06-30, `0000764065-26-000100`; `cover_shares.py` the same; 606,051,530 issued less 35,523,974 treasury = 570,527,556 on the balance sheet; the 75M shares sold at $12.69 on 2025-10-31 inside the count; no later issuing filing found); cap **$7,337M**; net debt **$8,035M** (debt $7,703M at 2026-06-30 plus finance leases $402M at 2025 year-end less cash $70M; operating leases, pension and OPEB, asset-retirement and Stelco trust payments left out). Sovereign **5.60%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-09). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (`0000764065-26-000025`), 10-K FY2022 (`0000764065-23-000032`), 10-Q to 2026-06-30, proxy 2026 (`0000764065-26-000054`), 8-K of 2026-07-24 (`0000764065-26-000102`); one figure cross-checked (2025 operating cash $(462)M against the filed statement). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the FY2025 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file (cost against the EAF producers, who sets the price, trade protection, debt and the capital raised, the acquisitions with pension and labor). Competitors: the 10-K names classes only, no rival by name; the analyst took Nucor, Steel Dynamics and U.S. Steel as a CONVENTION of the run, foreign producers and aluminum substitutes flagged as not compared. Q1 IN (an integrated steelmaker readable from its figures; Steelmaking 96% of 2025 revenue; the commodity paragraph of 2026-10-12 sends price and tariff to Q2 and Q7). **Q2 OUT, the high-cost producer in a commodity field**: pre-tax margin the lowest of the four in every year 2021 to 2025 and in H1 2026, 2.8% aggregate 2020 to 2025 against Nucor 16.3%, Steel Dynamics 15.9%, U.S. Steel 9.2% (2020 to 2024, FY2025 not found); a higher selling price ($1,005 a ton in 2025) with a lower margin, so a higher cost per ton, against the filer's claimed "inherent cost advantage"; 2025 Steelmaking gross margin (5)% with HRC up 10% under 50% tariffs; H1 2026 pre-tax (4.5)% after the slab contract ended against Steel Dynamics 10.6%; 60% to 65% of shipments at spot or index; six operations idled or closed in 2025. Q3 to Q12 not reached. After the stop: owner cash equity-only $1,906M, $1,282M, $1,421M, $(737)M, $(1,223)M (2021 to 2025); debt $3.1B (2023) to $7.7B (2026-06-30), cash never above $198M since 2020; retained earnings $1,733M (2023) to $(911)M; shares 271M (2019) to 570.5M; buybacks of 37.9M in 2024 at about $19.45, above every computed case, then 75M sold at $12.69 in 2025; an immaterial error corrected in the 2025 10-K (cost of goods sold understated 2022 to 2025); Adjusted EBITDA the featured and paid measure. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: cycle base 2020 to 2025 (both window ends aberrational, specific (a)), the AK Steel and ArcelorMittal USA merger averages not built, confessed; serial acquirer on Stelco, organic pair central; the series changes sign, so the range is the no-growth case alone; interest added back after tax at 25%, a CONVENTION of the run; range **$1.77 a share all-equity** ($9.63 literal window; equity-only $9.25 and $16.58) against $12.86; no case earns the floor (3.3% to 7.2%); fair **none positive all-equity** ($(5.21)), **equity-only $5.18**, computation only; no alert (box not OUT at Q7 or IN). Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the CFO, the CEO's son, named President and a director on 2026-07-21 with his severance multiple raised from two to three; CEO pay $19.0M in a year of a $1,428M net loss; the unsigned POSCO deal called "highly accretive". Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing filtered to today's date showed 27 other companies' run-file names, none for CLF, none opened; the session's git snapshot and memory index; none used. A 77 KB filing extract was committed in the Q1 commit and untracked in the Q2 commit by the analyst. Commits bef1f0c9, ffd65125, a8aff8f3, 3a1cb693. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for CLF or Cleveland-Cliffs). Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` passed; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_check.py` 39 ids, 21 quoted cites, no slip, no missing id, no E-id. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) the commodity paragraph's "its operators' filings" does not say which operators when the 10-K names only classes; (2) Q7(a)'s cycle base and (c)'s merger rule pull against each other when the cycle's first year is the merger year; (3) the serial-acquirer threshold is tripped by one large deal when owner cash nets to little; (4) the all-equity basis does not say whether interest is added back before or after tax. Could not get: cost per ton from each filer's segment note, Nucor's H1 2026, U.S. Steel's FY2025, finance leases at 2026-06-30, the pre-merger AK Steel figures.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: the integrated flat-rolled steelmaker whose pre-tax margin is the lowest of CLF, Nucor, Steel Dynamics and U.S. Steel in every year 2021 to 2025 and in H1 2026, 2.8% aggregate 2020 to 2025 against about 16% for the two EAF producers, with a higher selling price per ton, a (5)% Steelmaking gross margin in 2025 under 50% tariffs, and a pre-tax loss in H1 2026 after the slab contract ended. After the stop: debt $3.1B to $7.7B since 2023, buybacks at about $19.45 in 2024 then 75M shares sold at $12.69 in 2025. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range the no-growth case alone, $1.77 a share all-equity against $12.86, no case earns the floor, fair none positive all-equity, $5.18 equity-only. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the CEO's son made President and a director with a raised severance multiple; CEO pay $19.0M in a loss year.
